title: A cylindrical cell's end cap has twice the cylinder's radius and height about 0.27R

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A cylindrical cell's end cap has twice the cylinder's radius and height about 0.27R

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Where a cylindrical cell of uniform wall tension is capped by part of a sphere, the sphere's radius is twice the cylinder's radius, the cap subtends a cone of 60°, and its height is about 0.27 of the cylinder radius (a little more than one-eighth of the diameter), proportions seen in the free end cells of Spirogyra.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: R_{cap} = 2R; cap subtends a cone of 60^\circ; cap height = R(2 - \sqrt{3}) \approx 0.27R

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the normal height of the spherical cap over the end of the cylindrical cell is just a very little more than one-eighth of the diameter of the cylinder, or of the radius of the sphere. And these are the proportions which we recognise, under normal circumstances, in such a case as the cylindrical cell of Spirogyra where its free end is capped by a portion of a sphere.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Spherical caps on cylindrical cells”. Scope: cylindrical cells with free spherical ends, e.g. Spirogyra and other filamentous algae

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is an unusually precise and easily falsified geometric prediction. The analysis is simple, but a sufficiently large, calibrated public sample of the target cells is uncertain.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure cylinder radius, cap curvature radius, subtended angle, and cap height from calibrated 3D or optical images of free-ended Spirogyra cells. The law is supported if ratios cluster near 2 for sphere-to-cylinder radius and 0.27 for cap-height-to-cylinder-radius, with deviations linked to unequal tension.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
2D orientation biases cap measurements.

Open Spirogyra samples with calibration and free end cells are limited.

Wall anisotropy may violate the uniform-tension premise.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The cap proportions are a sharp geometric prediction and a poor fit would refute them. The raw material is public micrographs rather than a measurement table, so a test requires digitising ends, mainly of Spirogyra. That is feasible for a restricted scope and does not by itself show that uniform wall tension is the cause of whatever ratio is found.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On free end cells of Spirogyra and similar filaments, measure cylinder radius R and end-cap height, and test the predictions that cap height is about 0.27R and that the cap is a portion of a sphere of radius 2R subtending 60 degrees. A tight cluster around those values would support the claim; a mean far from 0.27R, or a cap radius other than 2R, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Turgor and wall thickness are not recorded with the photographs.

The numerical target assumes uniform wall tension, which may vary along the filament.

AlgaeBase images are illustrations, not a random sample of free end cells.
